Get started

Getting started with tidymapr

User guide

User guide

A complete guide to tidymapr: installation, concepts, code, figures, interpretation and reporting.

1. Install and run tidymapr in RStudio

Set up R, RStudio and tidymapr on Windows, macOS or Linux, make a first map and save it for a paper.

2. Cartography concepts: projections, classes and colour

The theory behind every design choice in a map, and how tidymapr makes and explains them.

3. Spatial autocorrelation: Moran's I, LISA and hot spots

Is there a spatial pattern, and where is it? Global and local statistics, how to read them and how to report them.

4. Interpolation: IDW and kriging

From samples to a continuous surface: variograms, kriging and its uncertainty, IDW, cross-validation and measurement error.

5. Species distribution models: Maxent and ensembles

Where can a species live? The theory of presence-background models, Maxent, ensembles, evaluation metrics, response curves and disagreement maps.

6. Remote sensing and terrain

Spectral indices, automatic thresholds, spectral diversity, D8 hydrology, the topographic wetness index and 3D terrain: concepts, maps and interpretation.

7. Point clusters and landscape fragmentation

DBSCAN clustering of point events, and FRAGSTATS landscape metrics: how they work, what each number means and how to report them.

8. Data in and out, occurrence cleaning, web maps and recipes

Read GIS, CAD, netCDF and spreadsheet data; download and clean GBIF records; share interactive web maps; run GeoSpaX recipes.

9. Distance decay and spatial eigenvectors

How similarity changes with distance, and how Moran’s eigenvector maps (dbMEM) turn space into predictors for models: concepts, interpretation and reporting.

10. Mid-domain effect on maps and in the sea

Could a richness hotspot arise from the shape of the land or the sea floor alone? Two- and three-dimensional mid-domain null models with geo_mde() and geo_mde_3d().
